concepts.title: Changing Composition of India's Trade
concepts.section: Changing Pattern of the Composition of India's Imports
concepts.definition: India's export composition shifted from agricultural products to manufactured goods, which formed about 67.8 per cent of exports in 2021-22, while imports include crude oil and petroleum, pearls, chemicals and electronic goods; the shift mirrors industrialisation and skill upgradation.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting the manufactured goods share of exports from 100 gives the share of agriculture, ores and other non-manufactured exports.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy208.txt export composition table (manufactured goods 67.8 per cent in 2021-22)

solution_steps.explain: manufactured goods formed about 67.8 per cent of exports

concepts.title: Direction and Balance of Trade
concepts.definition: India's trade direction has moved towards Asia: countries of Asia and ASEAN now take the largest shares of exports and imports, with the USA, China and Gulf states as leading partners, while the trade balance swings with oil prices and global demand.
concepts.key_idea: Neighbouring Asian economies replace old western partners as India's main trade geography, changing ports and shipping patterns too.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy208.txt direction of trade and major partners sections
question_patterns: which regions dominate India's trade direction

solution_steps.explain: Asian and ASEAN countries lead, with USA, China and Gulf states prominent
exports minus imports give the balance, favourable when positive
crude import bills swing the balance seasonally and cyclically

concepts.title: Sea Ports and Airports as Trade Gateways
concepts.definition: About 95 per cent of India's international trade by volume moves by sea through twelve major ports like Mumbai, Kandla, Visakhapatnam, Paradip and Chennai, complemented by minor ports and international airports handling high-value cargo like gems and electronics.
concepts.key_idea: Ports are trade's gateways: their capacity and turnaround decide whether export competitiveness reaches the seas.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy208.txt sea ports and airports sections

solution_steps.explain: about 95 per cent of trade volume rides the seas

gems, electronics and pharma prefer airports for speed and safety

concepts.title: Trade Policy and Global Integration
concepts.definition: India's trade policy moved from import substitution and licensing before 1991 to trade liberalisation, with reduced tariffs, export promotion zones and free trade agreements integrating India into global value chains.
concepts.key_idea: Liberalisation changed both what India trades and how: service exports, electronics assembly and regional agreements now shape the ledger.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy208.txt trade policy reform and export promotion sections
question_patterns: contrast pre-1991 and post-1991 trade policies

solution_steps.explain: 1991 liberalisation replaced licensing with tariff-led openness
export zones, FTAs and tariff cuts are the policy instruments
joining global value chains made ports and skills decisive
